summary: Douglas Co., WA tower built 1941 off national forest land near Wenatchee; cab moved in 1999 to the Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center at Entiat, where it sits by a public trail.

facts.status_note: The cab moved in 1999 to the Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center at Entiat. Sources do not say what became of the tower or whether anything remains on the mountain.

staffing.status: Named lookouts in 1930 and 1946 to 1974 (Basset, Calder, Poling, Richardson); FFLOS says the tower served the forest until the 1980s

access.note: The cab is at the Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center north of Entiat. A 2022 visit found the building closed but the parking area and interpretive trail open. The original mountain site was reached through private property, and no source describes access to it today.

events.note: May 1930 item: Richard Basset employed to attend the lookout station on Badger Mountain that season.
Tower built in 1941 per FFLOS and Firelookout. A 2022 visitor account says the cab was first built in the 1930s for Lion Rock (see resolved_conflicts).
Barbara Calder named as lookout for 1946 to 1947.
George Poling named as lookout for 1948 to 1950.
Oscar Richardson named as lookout for 1953 to 1974. No later staffing is named in the sources.
May 1961 newspaper item: Lowry Construction Co. was apparent low at $72,578 to build an unmanned gap filler facility, part of a radar installation near the Badger Mountain Lookout Station.
Cab moved to the Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center at Entiat.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register as US 1383, WA 283 on August 20, 2012.

corrections.current: None relocated (The lookout was moved to CBFIC.)
corrections.proposed: Cab moved in 1999 to the Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center at Entiat.
corrections.why: The brief's 'None relocated' contradicts its own note and the FFLOS record of the 1999 move.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and Firelookout give 1941 for the tower. The Roaming Civic says the cab was first built in the 1930s by the CCC for Lion Rock. Weebly's May 1930 item already describes a lookout station on Badger Mountain. The sources do not reconcile these, and the story reports the disagreement.

resolved_conflicts.field: number of lookouts at the Columbia Breaks center
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Visit Wenatchee says the center is built around two lookout towers. The Roaming Civic counts three relocated lookouts on the trail.
Firelookout gives 7 miles NNE of Wenatchee. The Weebly page, quoting a National Geodetic Survey description, gives 8 miles NNE.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 'None relocated' event wording is corrected above. The tower's own fate after the 1999 cab move is not in any source read. The 1961 notice and the 1930 item come from a Weebly page that quotes newspapers without naming the paper for every item. The Weebly header says 'Wenatchee - Okanogan National Forest' while FFLOS says 'Wenatchee National Forest'; the story follows FFLOS. The brief's source NHLR page for this site is not in the cache. Budget note: this tower went over the six-page-read budget (about 8 page reads including repeats) and used no WebSearch beyond the shared first search.
